summary:
Bullpen is the category to trust today — R1, R2, and R3 all carry 3-game winning streaks in that split, with R2 and R1 both sitting at 53% (100-90, n=190) over the last 14 days, well above their season baselines. SP is the opposite story: R3 SP is flagged cold at -5.2pts, and all three ratings are underwater in SP over the last 14 (86-104, 87-103, 45-46%), so any pick leaning heavily on starting pitcher edges — like STL @ CIN with McGreevy-Singer or ATL @ CHW's Holmes-Kay — deserves a discount unless bullpen or trends reinforce it. Strong-play units are bleeding across the board short-term: R1 is -15.0u over 7 days and -10.0u over 14, R2 -14.0u/-12.0u, R3 -12.0u/-13.0u, so don't chase strong-tagged plays blindly right now even though all three are comfortably profitable on the season (+12u, +13u, +23u).

Today's board leans heavily on consensus, and that's where the value sits. SEA @ MIL is the strongest signal of the day — all four ratings stack on MIL with R4 at +2.32 and R3 at +1.99, and MIL is a proven team-when-liked play at 62% (25-15) with strong-play units at +4.0u. STL @ CIN is the other full-strength consensus (all four ratings between -1.86 and -2.10 on STL), but with SP form cold league-wide and Singer on the mound for CIN, treat this more cautiously than the delta size suggests. TOR @ TBR is worth flagging for the intersection of a hot category and a great team: R3 and R4 both lean TBR near +1.2-1.3, and TBR is the best team-when-liked play on the board at 71% (25-10) with a monstrous +22.0u strong-play mark — if bullpen or trends confirm the lean pregame, this is the highest-confidence non-blowout play of the day. ATL @ CHW is the lone split (R3 breaks off to ATL at -0.20 while the rest lean CHW), so fade confidence there until a tiebreaker category clarifies it.
